questions.question: Read the following passage and answer the given questions accordingly: "Modern cities face a paradox. On one hand, technological innovations promise unprecedented efficiency in transport, communication, and energy use. On the other, these same innovations can deepen social divides if access remains limited to a privileged few. A city that invests heavily in digital infrastructure but neglects affordable housing and public healthcare risks becoming a polished shell with a fragile core. Sustainable urban development, therefore, is not merely a matter of constructing smart buildings or installing sensors on streetlights; it requires a deliberate effort to ensure that progress is broadly shared, particularly with those who have historically been excluded from its benefits." Q- Which of the following best captures the central idea of the passage?

questions.question: Read the following passage and answer the given questions accordingly: "For centuries, stories have been humanity’s preferred way of making sense of the world. Before scientific theories and statistical models, there were myths, legends, and folktales. Today, data may dominate boardroom presentations, yet narratives still guide decisions more than we care to admit. A neatly arranged spreadsheet can persuade, but a compelling story about a single customer’s struggle can transform a company’s strategy. The danger arises when stories are accepted uncritically: a vivid anecdote can overshadow large amounts of contradictory evidence, leading people to cling to beliefs that feel true rather than those that are well supported." Q- What is the primary concern expressed by the author in this passage?
